newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK disappointed at being put on U.S. watchlist.
newsitem.headline: HK disappointed at being put on U.S. watchlist.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Thursday it was disappointed with a U.S. decision to place it on a special watchlist aimed at copyright pirates.

"Given the considerable and persistent anti-piracy efforts and initiatives the government has made, we consider it most unjustified to place Hong Kong on the 'Watch List'," a government spokesman said in a statement.

The U.S. Information Service in Hong Kong confirmed that the U.S. Trade Representative's office had placed the territory on the Special 301 watch list on intellectual property rights (IPR) protection.
The Hong Kong government spokesman said customs had seized nearly one million copies of compact discs (CDs), VCDs, and CD-ROMs last year, a rise of 164 percent from 1995.
Tighter legislation against piracy would be introduced while the industry is also working to fight against copyright infringement, he said.
The government has established a liaison network with IPR enforcement authorities in China to stop pirated products from entering Hong Kong, the spokesman said.
"Courts are also handing down much heavier penalties for persons convicted of copyright piracy," he said.
A persistently poor record could merit possible U.S. trade sanctions.
Hong Kong is heavily dependent on trade with the United States, which is its main trading partner after China.
